_note: Pinned model, not '-latest': a moving alias would change the voice mid-experiment. posts_per_trend 3 so one run yields ~10-12 candidates and --auto 6 is still the top half — see generate.yml for the backlog arithmetic.
_note_repo: Where the buttons on the Pages site file their commands. The site is static and this repo is public, so a page cannot hold a token — a prefilled issue is the one way a tap becomes a workflow with no secret in the HTML. See control.py.
_note_windows: Windows, not instants, and the deadline is the part that moved. GitHub does not deliver the cron it is given: from 2026-09-18 12:58 to 18:19 the */20 publish poll was due ~16 times and ran ONCE, and generate's schedule has fired once in its life. The 15:00-17:00 window was missed outright with a post sitting in the queue. So 'after' is still the researched best time and nothing publishes before it — 'before' is now hours later, because a window only catches a poll if it is wide enough to be hit. min_publish_gap_minutes is the cost of that: widening the deadlines put the end of one window within an hour of the next window's start, and two posts in one hour compete for the same audience. --now ignores it. A fixed UTC offset rather than a timezone name because IST has no DST.
